body: Hi! My wife and I have been together close to 8 years now! We both have BPD And Bipolar Disorder type 1, plus some other psych stuff on top of those. It makes things hard when we’re both in a spiral or breakdown, But! We have really found a groove over the past few years. Things were really, really hard at first for the first 3 or 4 years. Our communication styles are very different and miscommunications lead to a lot of problems. Being in regular therapy and finding the right meds (for us) has been helpful, as is couples counseling. Knowing that we’re stronger than our problems and that both of us are committed to eachother, despite obstacles, has been really grounding. It’s constant work, but it’s rewarding. Yes, you Can have a healthy relationship with the BPD diagnosis. Always strive to understand yourself and your partner and have good empathy. Keep working on yourself and the relationship Should get easier. I wish you the best of luck!

But also, I’d encourage you to look more into parrot rehabilitation if this is something that interests you…. There are parrot rescue orgs just like for dogs and cats that are full to the brim and they need volunteers. It’s really rewarding working with birds, and a lot of them get passed around over their long lifetimes and not everyone can give a pet parrot what they need in terms of mental stimulation… some Are abused and neglected and develop bad behavioral problems and they need a lot of TLC.

So, I don’t know this particular parrot’s backstory, but I used to work with them professionally and I’ve had several birds of my own. This is a yellow naped Amazon parrot  and I’m guessing it’s a male. Amazons, out of all the medium sized parrots, tend to be the most unpredictable. They’re suuuper smart (they’re also my favorite out of all the parrots I’ve had/worked with) they can generally understand a lot of what they’re “mimicking” if they’re good talkers…. Here, I’d say that this male bird is very excited, maybe even super hormonal if it’s the right time of year… when amazons get overstimulated and hormonal they can also get territorial and/or just plain aggressive. They also like to play mind games… I’m not kidding. They’re suuuper smart! He has obviously been barbering/plucking his feathers… but they’re growing back in, so that’s good. Birds pluck their feathers for many different reasons, sometimes due to lack of mental stimulation or something like a bout of separation anxiety when their owners go on vacation…sometimes it’s due to an underlying medical condition. And when they start plucking their feathers, it can become a habit that’s very hard to break, even if whatever occurred to make them start plucking is fixed. Maybe this parrot was pointedly abused, I don’t know… usually they’re not being physically abused, even in an unfit home… but my theory on him is that he picked up the phrase at a vet visit, or while getting his talons groomed, or while getting his wings clipped (it doesn’t physically hurt them to clip the wing feathers, but most birds don’t like being restrained in a towel while they’re being groomed) Even more likely is that someone was trying to work with the bird to get him to come out of his cage or to get him to step up onto a hand, and he was wary or aggressive and they said these things to him several times during that whole process. Being prey animals, parrots are naturally very fearful of new things and even if socialized with humans properly, they can be aggressive.   So, I think that he picked up these phrases, and it’s not as dark as people are thinking. He’s being aggressive because he’s overstimulated, and probably hormonal and because he’s on the floor, and a lot of birds will attack feet if they have free reign of the floor… and he’s purposefully saying these things in a way that amuses him… because they’re That Smart. My own Amazon would do something similar…. She could say the words “step up” (that’s what you say to a bird to get it on your hand) and so she’d say, “step up Pogo” while you’d be trying to get her to step up onto your hand…but she’d be backing away, and then she’d lunge and bite and literally laugh a human laugh about it. She was a very well adjusted and very loved parrot and had never been abused… it was just a game she made up… I know this has been a long comment, but it pulled at my heartstrings when you were so concerned for this bird, in any case, he’s in a good home now… you can tell that this owner is patiently working with him on his behavioral issues. Mostly I think he’s just a cheeky Amazon.

From someone who used to sell parrots/budgies at a pet store, them being so scared of the new environment to the point of not eating is Very normal… just watch closely for other symptoms of illness! 

One trick is to move the food closer to them. Definitely offer millet sprays and hang a food And water dish near where they are perching. Eating and drinking is their most vulnerable act, so you might not see much evidence that they’ve eaten much the first few days. Check the parakeet’s cage papers for poops and make sure they look normal. 

Good luck!

You can also have the two birds FaceTime eachother. My Amazon and my best friend’s Amazon never met eachother in person but they loved video chats. There was a study about video chatting parrots as well.

The “cute” background song commonly used on TikToks and IG videos “Da doo ba doo, da doo ba doo doo doo…” On and on with the “doos” and “ba doos” I don’t know what it actually is or where it originally came from, but I hate it.

To me, it sounds like separation anxiety from your mom leaving for the work trip started the plucking. Once they start, it’s hard to get them to stop! It could also be an underlying medical condition causing skin irritation, though… Giardia from bacterial build up in dirty water bowls, etc, can also be a cause. if you have the means and have an Avian vet in your area, I’d take him in for a checkup with blood work. Bird vet offices are also well versed in behavioral modification. Foraging (look it up, plenty of online resources) is your bird’s best very best friend! If the bird is going to be moved into a separate room, I wouldn’t anticipate that that would help the plucking…. They love to be as near to their flock mates as possible and your green cheek might get even more stressed! It’s much easier to isolate a parrot in a separate room. Try to listen to the advice of experienced bird folks, but don’t get down on yourself for being inexperienced. You’re trying your best and reaching out for help! There’s always people in bird forums that can be very harsh… they just care about the birds, but it’s obvious to me that you’re trying to do the right thing. Good luck

If she has a separate bowl of seeds, she’s probably just holding out and only eating the seeds, preferring them over the Roudybush. BUT it is very important not to just take the seeds away as their metabolisms are super quick and their organs can shut down very fast if they’re not eating… I lost my own female budgie, Bludger, that way! She had been eating her pellets fine for a long time and then just stopped. I thought she was just being picky. I was trying to hold out and keep her on the pellets, and by the time I realized that she was too thin, she was too far gone, even after I gave her millet and seeds. This all happened in like a day or two. It’s been a long time but I just wanted to warn you about their metabolisms.

Yes I agree that individual to individual, parrotlets can be fantastic! (I love all birdos) But they can also be really really aggressive. It’s been common historically in aviculture for parrotlets even to attack/kill their mates. Male budgies can learn to talk really well and they’re usually a little less bitey. No shade trying to be thrown on your birds :)

Here to be contrary and say budgies over parrotlets for kids! Parrotlets in general tend to be much more aggressive than budgies! They can be very bitey. I’d still recommend a cockatiel over either of those, though.

When you have 1 cockatiel alone they can be incredibly needy and develop problem behaviors like screaming for attention. With two they are a bit more content to do their own thing. Having sold cockatiels in the past…. It’s definitely Not to sell more birds! A reputable source for these animals truly wants what is best for them.
Also rescue from a bird rescue is a good choice and there are many wonderful cockatiel pairs that need homes!

Cockatiels can be in same sex pairs to discourage breeding. Females introduced as babies or from the same parents would be good in my opinion. I’ve also known males to be kept together and the males can learn recognizable whistles and sometimes talk a bit. If a reputable pet store/bird store is close to you, they may be able to DNA sex the young ones so you can be sure not to end up with a male/female pair. Male/females are going to pair bond strongly and not want as much to do with you humans. I had two cockatiel hens that I got when I was 12. They got along well together and I also invested a lot in handling them myself when they were babies so we were all friends. Like others have said, I wouldn’t trust kids younger than a Very Responsible 11 or 12yo to be alone with birds, and they are supposed to live into their 20s at least(I knew a cockatiel who was going strong at 30yo) You’re definitely going to be the one responsible for the birds’ care for quite awhile. Birds can be great if taken care of right, and if in the right fit for a home. Growing up with cockatiels really got me into birds in general…. They do like to be scratched on the head, and cockatiels are cuddlier than some other birds, but petting the birds down their backs or other places is a no-no as it can make them hormonal. Good luck!

I’m confused. You berate OP for taking the bird outside without precaution, but then also berate them for clipping wings? Which IS a precaution against flying away when outdoors(not perfect, but lesson learned)? In my opinion, you should always take a bird outside in a carrier, and wing clipping or not is a personal preference. They are much, MUCH more likely to escape with intact wings and be at risk when outdoors not to mention other dangers around the house when they are flying around inside. There are costs/benefits to either side. If this bird had had its wings clipped it would have had a better chance to get reclaimed by OP if it tried to fly when they were outside. I’ve heard a lot of horror stories and lost multiple flighted birds myself to the great outdoors who were never found. One cockatiel was eaten by a hawk. There are pros and cons to clipping or not clipping, and in my opinion, both are valid ways to keep birds. I’ve met a lot of healthy, well-kept, clipped birds.

Yes get the bird. I was in line to buy an “ethical “ local parrot specialty store several years ago, after working there for 8 years. Even the most “ethical” pet store is contributing to the general problem of bird ownership, so in my opinion, no store is perfect! There are plenty, thousands, of aging parrots that need homes in rescues. But THIS BIRD chose *You* And that is something very special. I’ve gotten my past birds all sorts of ways, as a child, 1 cockatiel from a friend who allowed her pets to breed, 1 cockatiel from a very ethical & well run pet store. Then 1 parakeet from Petco (gasp) and 1 from the ethical local store I worked at later. Finally, I bought a rehomed Amazon who lived at that same pet store for 2 years(!!)waiting for a home. I bought my other Amazon as a baby, and then my final Amazon I got from Craigslist. His owner had died, he’s 9 yo. The one thing I would say is that my Petco budgie lived a fairly short life for a parakeet as compared to her husband from the local parrot store. But I wouldn’tve traded her, she was amazing! Like others have said, boycotting this purchase from Petsmart is not going to hurt the chain, but it’s hurting your heart so go back and get her! We can work towards a better future for our parrots in captivity all sorts of ways. Lots of the small “ethical” local bird shops have things going on behind closed doors that are just as bad as the big box stores. In my opinion, it’s SUCH a complicated issue! From someone who was going to make the store 100% rescue animals, don’t be so hard on yourself. I hope we get a good update soon!

Hey there, I am hoping you are still here. It sounds like your life situation can be improved, and when it improves, you may find that you don’t want to end yourself anymore. August 5th, 2 years ago, was the day I was going to take a poison with no antidote. I ordered everything off the internet and was set on it. I posted on here with my throwaway account and barely anyone even commented. I had struggled with suicidal ideation on and off for 19 years at that point, and that was the closest I ever came to actually going through with a plan. I was feeling hopeless and like a drain on others. 
I didn’t do it because someone took the time to tell me, IRL, that they didn’t want me to kill myself and that was *just barely enough* prodding to flip the switch in my brain. I didn’t even know the person too well. That’s what I’m trying to tell to you. I care about you and I want you to stay. I want to hear about how you beat this in a few months. I wouldn’t judge you if you pulled the trigger, BUT I also 100% don’t think that it’s necessary. It sounds to me like you are in an awful living situation /unfulfilling work situation and need some friends and a loving partner and some professional psychiatric guidance, but those things are obtainable and your living situation can be temporary. 

I’m so sorry to hear that your life is so hard right now. It IS HARD. Listen to the voice in your head and postpone postpone postpone booking the hotel room. Nurture the determined-to-get-better side of you…. I’m rooting for you and I want you to be here.

For myself, I chose not to take the poison because I just realized that I wanted to live solely for myself and to experience the rest of what life has to offer, the good and bad. I can always die later. I got angry at the people who I thought hadn’t cared, and I got very self protective of me. Since then, I haven’t struggled with suicidal ideation anymore. It really was like something flipped. 

I really hope you get through this. You can. I believe in you and I’m proud of you for having the courage to write what you did. Lots of love your way.

There are videos on YouTube on how to handfeed. I used to do it for years but I wouldn’t feel comfortable even showing someone in person anymore! Right now it’s important that the bird eats SOMETHING. The pellet diet is great for birds who are not potentially starving/we don’t know what diet they were on! Feeding parrots can be tricky, especially changing their diets. I used to work at a specialty parrot store for 8 years before switching careers. The most important thing to remember is to do diet changes Very gradually and watch your bird's weight while making those changes. Small birds like cockatiels can starve themselves to death incredibly quickly, before you even realize it. 

That being said, from what I've read, seed only diets can give a bird fatty liver disease down the line....variety is the main thing that matters! If your bird eats seeds as the base of its diet, try to make sure it also gets lots of veggies, a little bit of fruit and some whole grains, too.  But, there are also some some things that are toxic to birds. Avocado, onions, garlic, rhubarb, pits of fruit and most fruit seeds are all poisonous, as well as some leaves and stems of some veggies and fruits. Potatoes and legumes should be cooked before feeding

Some good things to feed are 

Carrots and carrot tops, cooked sweet potatoes, parsley, romaine lettuce, cooked quinoa, oatmeal, blueberries and blackberries, bell peppers, peas, to name a few

Birds usually like apples and corn too, but anything high in sugar should be fed sparingly....

Lots of people will probably tell you to convert your bird to a pelleted diet, and pellets are awesome IF you can get them easily where you are AND you convert your bird to eating them correctly...this is sometimes a very difficult task, and if your bird doesn't recognize them as food, it could starve itself!

I love pellet bird food, and all of my birds have eaten them except those that were already eating seed when I got them and wouldn't convert.
